question: Public procurement is a critical part of the EU’s economic framework, accounting for approximately 14 % of its GDP. In this connection, it is vital to ensure that taxpayers’ money is well spent and to increase the level of competitiveness in the EU.

Findings from a recent audit1 by the European Court of Auditors highlight that in the past decade, there has been a noticeable decline in the level of competition in public procurement within the single market. This trend is concerning, given the significant potential for public procurement to drive economic growth and innovation.
The 2014 Public Procurement Directives have not had the expected impact, as there has been relatively little change in the share of SMEs participating in public procurement processes. 1.
How does the Commission plan to address the significant differences in procurement practices between Member States, as outlined in the report?

What specific action – including measures to streamline application procedures, reduce administrative burdens and ensure fair competition – will the Commission take to break down the barriers faced by SMEs in public procurement, and how will this be evaluated?
How will the Commission promote the use of award criteria other than price to encourage strategic procurement practices that take account of environmental, social or innovation aspects?

European Court of Auditors Special Report 28/2023, ‘Public procurement in the EU – Less competition for contracts awarded for works, goods and services in the 10 years up to 2021’, 4 December 2023, https://www.eca.europa.eu/ECAPublications/SR-2023-28/SR-2023-28_EN.pdf.
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (2.10.2024) The Commission welcomed the European Court of Auditors’ (ECA) special report on public procurement1 and accepted all the recommendations it formulated2.

As mentioned in its reply, the Commission will analyse the causes of substantial shortcomings in public procurement markets, including obstacles to the participation of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) to tenders and will work towards the revision of the directives announced by the President-elect of the Commission in the political guidelines 2024-20293.

In this complex process, all stakeholders will be given the opportunity to express their views and provide input. Additionally, the Commission will continue to pursue initiatives to support the use of sustainability and innovation considerations in public procurement.

These include fostering communities of practice of public buyers across the EU4 and organising government dialogues in the Member States for the creation of national strategies to implement strategic procurement.
